name: Burg Landeck
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Landeck perches on a rocky spur above the Inn: built in 1250, sovereign court seat, 1522 Gothic chapel, and regional museum.
beschreibung:
Overview

The prominent Schloss Landeck (also known as Burg Landeck) sits atop a steeply sloping rock spur high above the district capital of Landeck in the Tyrolean Oberland at 817 metres above sea level. An unmistakable landmark of the town, this fortress guarded the strategic crossroads of three major Alpine passes (Arlberg, Reschenpass, Fernpass) since the High Middle Ages. Today, the carefully restored castle houses the award-winning Bezirksmuseum Landeck, a prestigious art gallery, and a lively cultural centre.

History & Architecture

The castle was built in the first half of the 13th century?presumably around 1250?by the Grafen von Ulten along the ancient route of the Via Claudia Augusta. Following the extinction of the Counts of Ulten, Count Meinhard II. von Tirol-G?rz extensively fortified the complex around 1290; from 1282 onwards, the castle served as an important provincial court of justice. The complex enjoyed its architectural golden age during the 15th and 16th centuries under the Knights of Schrofenstein: during this era, the late-Gothic castle chapel Burgkapelle zum Hl. Stephanus was built, boasting precious wall frescoes from 1522 depicting St. Stephen and Archangel Michael. Historical features include the imposing keep, a three-storey palas residence, and an idyllic Gothic arcaded courtyard. Following exemplary restoration by the Verein Schloss Landeck, the regional museum was awarded the Austrian Museum Quality Seal. The centerpiece of the permanent exhibition 'Bleiben oder Gehen' focuses on the touching fate of the legendary Schwabenkinder?Tyrolean farm children who migrated to Swabia for seasonal summer farm work in the 19th century.

Visit & Getting There

The district museum is open in the summer season (25 April to 26 October) daily from 10:00 to 17:00 (no closing days). In the winter season (mid-December to 6 January), the museum opens daily from 13:00 to 17:00 (closed on 1 January). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults ?9.00, seniors ?8.00, visitors with disabilities ?5.00, pupils and students ?4.50, children under 6 free. Family tickets range from ?12.00 to ?19.00. Admission is free with the TirolWest Card guest card. Arrival by train: ?BB express service to Landeck-Zams station, from where local city bus (line 2 or 3) runs to the Stadtpfarrkirche church, followed by an approx. 10 to 15-minute walk uphill to the castle. By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 or Arlbergschnellstra?e S16 to Landeck; parking in the valley at the Innparkplatz or short-stay parking near the Volksschule / Stadtpfarrkirche.

Tips

The castle courtyard and ground floor with accessible toilet offer barrier-free, step-free access; exhibition spaces in the tower and upper floors are reached via historic wooden stairs. The permanent exhibition on the Schwabenkinder provides a deeply moving insight into Alpine social history. From the castle garden, enjoy a magnificent vista overlooking the valley basins of Landeck and Zams as well as the Lechtaler Alpen.
oeffnungszeiten: Sommer täglich 10:00–17:00 Uhr, Winter tgl. 13:00–17:00 Uhr
